faq.question: What products do you offer?
faq.answer: Three products built for schools: the CBT Examination System, the Question Bank and the School Management System. Each works on its own, and they are designed to work together as a suite.

faq.question: Can I request a demo?
faq.answer: Yes — that's the best way to start. Fill in the demo request form or send us a WhatsApp message, and we'll arrange a walkthrough at a time that suits your school.

faq.question: Can my school start with just one product?
faq.answer: Yes. Most schools start with the product that solves their most pressing problem — often CBT or the Question Bank — and add the others later.

faq.question: Can we use all three products together?
faq.answer: Yes. The products are designed as a suite: for example, questions from the Question Bank feed straight into CBT examinations, and the School Management System holds the student and class records behind them.

faq.question: Is the system suitable for primary schools?
faq.answer: Yes — the products are designed with both primary and secondary schools in mind, and we tailor the walkthrough to your school level during the demo.

faq.question: Is it suitable for secondary schools?
faq.answer: Yes — computer-based testing, a structured question bank and central record-keeping are a natural fit for secondary schools preparing students for external examinations.

faq.question: How does CBT work?
faq.answer: Staff prepare questions and set the exam duration in advance. On exam day, students sign in on a computer, answer on screen and submit. Objective questions are marked automatically and results are available immediately.

faq.question: Can teachers create questions?
faq.answer: Yes — the Question Bank is built for teachers to create, edit and organise questions by subject and class, so your school's questions stay with the school.

faq.question: How are results generated?
faq.answer: In the CBT system, objective questions are marked automatically and scores appear as soon as an exam is submitted. In the School Management System, results are compiled per student, subject and term. We'll show you both during your demo.

faq.question: Can the system work without internet?
faq.answer: Yes — SkulSuite has an offline edition that runs on your school's own network: one server computer plus the router the school already has. Exams, attendance, records and report cards all work without internet; a short phone-hotspot session about once a month handles updates and backups. See the Offline or Online page for the full comparison.

faq.question: How much does it cost?
faq.answer: Pricing depends on your school's size and needs, so we don't publish fixed prices. Request a demo or contact us, and we'll put together the right package for your school.

faq.question: Do you provide setup assistance and training?
faq.answer: Yes — we work with your school through setup and staff training so your team is comfortable from day one. The exact support package is confirmed when you request a demo.

faq.question: Can the system be customised for our school?
faq.answer: Schools differ, so we discuss your specific needs during the demo and confirm what can be tailored to the way your school works.

offlineEdition.summary: SkulSuite runs with or without internet. The offline edition runs on the school's own network (one server computer + the school's router; no internet day-to-day; a short phone-hotspot session about once a month handles updates, licence checks and backups). The online edition runs on cloud servers so parents and staff connect from anywhere. Licence prices are the same in both editions; offline removes yearly hosting and domain fees and adds the one-time ₦50,000 setup and offline installation fee.

requirements.detail: A single dedicated computer (even a normal desktop) holds the software and the school's data. It does not need to be powerful or new.
The same Wi-Fi router or network switch many schools already own connects the exam computers and phones to the server. No internet subscription is involved.
A small UPS or inverter on the server computer keeps an exam from stopping mid-way when power cuts. This matters more offline than anything else.
About once a month, someone connects the server to a phone hotspot for a few minutes — that handles software updates, licence checks and an off-site backup copy.
A cheap external drive kept in the school office holds a daily backup copy, so records survive even a failed computer.

faqs.question: Can SkulSuite really run without internet?
faqs.answer: Yes. The offline edition runs on the school's own network: one server computer plus the router the school already has. Exams, attendance, records and report cards all work without any internet. About once a month, a short phone-hotspot session handles updates, licence checks and backups.

faqs.question: How do CBT exams work offline on exam day?
faqs.answer: The exam computers and phones connect to the school's server through the school's own network — no internet involved. Students answer on screen with autosave, questions can be shuffled per student, and objective scores appear the moment each student submits, exactly as on the online edition.

faqs.question: If there's no internet, how do parents see results?
faqs.answer: On the offline edition, parents see results when they visit the school, and the school prints report cards as usual. If parents following results from home is important to your school, the online edition (or moving online later) is the better fit.

faqs.question: What happens if we start offline and want to go online later?
faqs.answer: Your records move with you. Both editions are the same products — the offline edition simply keeps the data on a school server instead of cloud servers. Schools often start offline and add the online edition when they're ready; we migrate the data during setup.

faqs.question: Does the offline edition cost less?
faqs.answer: It removes the yearly cloud hosting and domain fees (₦130,000–₦525,000 + ₦40,000 a year online), and adds the one-time ₦50,000 setup and offline installation fee. Software licence prices are the same. See the cost comparison above for the full picture.

faqs.question: What does the school need to provide?
faqs.answer: One computer to act as the server, the router or switch the school likely already owns, power backup (a small UPS) for that server, and an external drive for daily backups. We handle installation, configuration and staff training.

faqs.question: Who installs and trains our staff?
faqs.answer: We do — that's what the setup and offline installation fee covers, at one school site. A staff training session (₦20,000) gets your teachers confident from day one.

faqs.question: Is our data safe on one computer?
faqs.answer: It's protected two ways: the system keeps a daily backup copy on an external drive the school holds, and the monthly hotspot session also sends an off-site backup copy. The school owns its data in both editions.
